seoTitle: How to Buy Coursera Plus: Plans and Pricing Guide
metaDescription: Walk through buying Coursera Plus step by step, from comparing plans and pricing to completing checkout for unlimited access to thousands of courses.
intro: Coursera Plus bundles thousands of courses, Specializations, and Professional Certificates into one subscription, but the buying process has a few decision points that aren't obvious the first time through. You need to find the right entry point on Coursera, understand what the subscription actually covers before you pay for it, and pick between the monthly and annual pricing. This guide walks through each of those steps using the real Coursera pages you'll land on, from the initial search through checking your account once the subscription is active, so you know exactly what to expect at every screen.

steps.heading: Search for Coursera and open the official site
steps.body: Start with a plain search for "coursera" rather than following a link from an ad or a random article, since that's the safest way to land on the real coursera.org domain. The results page also surfaces useful shortcuts straight away — a direct link to Coursera Plus, a link for logging into an existing account, and a "Free Courses" result if you're not sure you want to commit to a paid plan yet. Click through to the main Coursera link to reach the homepage, or go straight to the Coursera Plus result if you already know that's the subscription you want.

image.caption: A search for "coursera" surfaces the official site along with direct shortcuts to Coursera Plus and the account login page.

steps.heading: Sign in and find your account menu
steps.body: Log into Coursera with your email or a connected account like Google. Once you're signed in, the top-right corner of the screen holds a profile icon that opens a menu listing My Learning, My Purchases, Settings, Updates, and Help Center. This is also where any active subscription shows up — the menu displays your current plan right at the top, so it's worth checking here first if you're not sure whether you already have Coursera Plus running under a different email or a free trial you forgot about. Knowing this menu exists now saves you a search later when you want to manage billing or check your renewal date.

image.caption: The account menu in the top-right corner shows your current subscription status alongside My Learning, My Purchases, and Settings.

steps.heading: Understand what the subscription actually includes
steps.body: Before entering any payment details, it's worth reading through what Coursera Plus covers, since not every course on the platform is included. The subscription bundles access to the majority of courses, guided projects, and Specializations from university and industry partners, and it lets you switch between courses without paying again if one turns out not to be a good fit. It does not typically cover standalone Professional Certificates from certain partners or full online degree programs, which are usually priced and purchased separately.

image.caption: Coursera Plus's frequently asked questions section, covering what's included, certificate limits, and employer reimbursement.

steps.heading: Check the FAQ for certificate and reimbursement details
steps.body: The same FAQ section answers a handful of questions that matter more than they first appear. It covers how many certificates you can earn while subscribed, what you're allowed to do with a certificate after you've earned it, and whether Coursera Plus purchases are commonly reimbursed by employers running professional development budgets. It also explains what happens to any Specialization you were already paying for individually if you subscribe to Coursera Plus afterward, which matters if you're mid-course and considering the switch.

steps.heading: Compare the monthly and annual pricing
steps.body: Coursera Plus is typically sold as either a monthly or an annual subscription, with the annual option working out cheaper per month in exchange for paying the full year upfront. If you're only testing the waters with one or two courses, the monthly plan limits your commitment and is easy to cancel once you're done. If you already know you'll be working through multiple Specializations over the coming months, the annual plan is usually the better value, and Coursera often prompts you with the savings difference directly on the pricing page.

steps.heading: Select a plan and complete checkout
steps.body: Once you've picked monthly or annual, proceed to checkout and enter your payment details. Coursera will confirm the plan, price, and billing cycle before you finalize the purchase, so double-check the renewal date and price shown match what you intended to sign up for. After payment goes through, your subscription activates immediately and the account menu you checked earlier will reflect the new plan.

steps.heading: Start browsing your unlimited course access
steps.body: With Coursera Plus active, head to My Learning or the course catalog to start enrolling. There's no extra checkout step for individual courses covered by the subscription — you enroll directly and start immediately. Since switching between courses costs nothing extra, it's worth sampling the first module of a few different options before committing your full attention to one, especially if you're weighing multiple Specializations against each other.

faq.question: What's included with a Coursera Plus subscription?
faq.answer: It gives you unlimited access to the majority of courses, guided projects, and Specializations on the platform, though some standalone Professional Certificates and full degree programs are typically sold separately.

faq.question: Are there different pricing tiers to choose from?
faq.answer: Yes — Coursera Plus is generally offered as a monthly or an annual subscription, with the annual plan working out cheaper per month in exchange for paying upfront.

faq.question: Is Coursera Plus worth it for someone taking just one course?
faq.answer: If you only need a single course, a one-off purchase may cost less than a subscription. Coursera Plus pays off once you plan to take several courses or switch between Specializations.

faq.question: Can I use Coursera Plus for career-focused learning?
faq.answer: Yes, the subscription is commonly used by professionals and students building skills across business, technology, and other in-demand fields, and many employers reimburse the cost as professional development.

faq.question: How do I check whether I already have a Coursera Plus subscription?
faq.answer: Sign in and open the account menu in the top-right corner of any Coursera page — your current subscription, if any, is displayed at the top of that menu.
